newsitem.title: BELGIUM: France committed to EMU, jobs summit vital - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: France committed to EMU, jobs summit vital - Chirac.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Thursday that France was totally determined to launch a single European currency on time, within the terms fixed by the Maastricht treaty.
In a speech to the European Commission during a state visit to Brussels, he also said that a European Union jobs summit due later this year was of vital importance to France.
France's new Socialist-led government has insisted that the EU give greater priority to economic policies that boost jobs as it moves towards its planned single currency in 1999.

Its opposition to tougher austerity to fulfil a strict reading of Maastricht treaty criteria has raised some questions about how far it is prepared to go to ensure a single currency is launched on time.

"France's commitments are clear. It is totally determined to launch the single currency on January 1, 1999, within the terms fixed by the (Maastricht) treaty," the conservative Chirac said. A copy of his speech was distributed to reporters.
In a gesture of support for the French government's jobs drive, he said that "the success of the special European summit on employment is of major importance to France".
